text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: realtime-latency-detector alert - p99 = 1.92s over the last 5m for prod (model=redwood-compact-v2). SLO window approaching breach. Auto-page sent to oncall.

maya (oncall): ACK. I'm taking pager. pulling dashboards now -> link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/latency/realtime

devon (eng-sre): I see the same on traces. p95 up ~40%, p99 spike concentrated on streaming endpoints (/v1/stream). KV cache miss rate jumped ~3x at 12:40 UTC.

sam (runtime): There was a small kernel/gradual rollout to runtime nodes ~8m before alert. rolling->kernel-2.1.4. putting hypothesis: rollout introduced scheduling hiccup or changed batch sizing.

maya (oncall): timeline: alert 1769456789, rollout finished ~1769456100, first customer 504s reported ~1769456600. I'm going to: 1) pause rollout (if still running), 2) enable fallback route to latency-optimized variant, 3) scale up workers.

ops-bot: scaling: pool:redwood-runtime-64g desired=4 -> 8 (initiated).

sam (runtime): paused rollout. also toggled batching_override=0.5 to reduce head-of-line blocking. watch for token-per-request regression.

devon (eng-sre): quick probe logs (last 2m):
```
[2026-05-04T12:41:02Z] req_id=abc123 model=compact-v2 duration=1920ms queue_ms=1100 kernel_wait=760 kv_cache_hit=false
[2026-05-04T12:41:11Z] req_id=abc125 model=compact-v2 duration=1840ms queue_ms=980 kernel_wait=720 kv_cache_hit=false
[2026-05-04T12:42:05Z] req_id=abc129 model=compact-v2 duration=2100ms queue_ms=1320 kernel_wait=750 kv_cache_hit=false
```

devon (eng-sre): looks like queue_ms is the main contributor. worker CPU not pegged, but libdispatch queue depth went up. also seeing one-off serialization stalls in runtime logs.

carla (support): Seeing customer reports from EU cluster - ~15 sessions got transient 5xx (504) starting ~12:41. No billing-impacting errors, but degraded UX. Customers A and D opened tickets.

maya (oncall): mitigation steps taken: paused rollout (sam), scaled pool to 8 (ops-bot), enabled route->redwood-compact-lite for latency-sensitive traffic (feature-flag). I'm also opening an incident page: https://console.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-042 (status: mitigation).

sam (runtime): small experiment: toggled streaming_chunk_mode=chunked for /v1/stream endpoints to avoid long-lived single-message stalls. Monitoring client-side error rates.

devon (eng-sre): traces after mitigation look better for new requests routed to compact-lite: p99 ~ 560ms. For remaining compact-v2 routed traffic, p99 still ~1.6-1.9s. Need to investigate kernel-2.1.4 path and batching changes.

maya (oncall): paging opa-team and runtime lead for deeper dive, but for now primary mitigation is routing + scale. @carla can you confirm and post if customers still seeing errors?

carla (support): Confirmed: after routing change, support saw error rate drop by ~80% for affected sessions. Two customers still report occasional stalls, but overall impact reduced.

sam (runtime): grabbing runtime pod logs and core dump on one node that showed serialization stack. cc: @devon.

devon (eng-sre): quick diagnostic checklist I'm running:
- compare kernel-2.1.3 vs 2.1.4 latency profiles
- KV cache telemetry correlation (misses vs p99)
- per-pod queue_depth and dispatch latency histograms
- examine recent NGINX connection reset patterns for streaming route

maya (oncall): Are we gating rollback? If kernel-2.1.4 is root cause we should roll back to 2.1.3; need vote from runtime + eng-sre.

sam (runtime): I can cut rollback to 2.1.3 in a canary then promote if green. ETA ~7m for canary, 20m for full rollback.

devon (eng-sre): I support rollback given queue_ms signals. do it canary first + watch p99 and queue_ms.

incident-bot: Note: next escalation in 12 minutes if p99 > 1.5s continues.

maya (oncall): assigning follow-ups: sam (runtime) - canary rollback + confirm; devon (eng-sre) - root cause on queueing + KV cache correlation; carla (support) - customer comms + status updates; I'll sit as incident lead and prepare handoff post-stabilization.

carla (support): posting a short message to affected customers now with steps we took and ETA for next update.

sam (runtime): canary rollback started at 1769456900 on 2 nodes. monitoring metrics.

devon (eng-sre): canary shows queue_ms drop to ~200ms and p99 ~620ms within 90s. Initial canary green.

maya (oncall): great. Proceed with progressive rollback. Please incrementally promote. Keep this thread for updates. We'll handoff after sustained 30m of p99 under 700ms.

sam (runtime): progressive rollback in flight. I'll post timestamps as nodes switch.

devon (eng-sre): logging next steps and artifacts in incident doc: https://console.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-042/artifacts (kernel perf diffs, KV cache histograms, pod logs).

maya (oncall): thanks everyone. if anything regresses ping @channel. setting reminder to handoff in 35m.

ops-bot: autoscale: pool:redwood-runtime-64g scaled to 8 healthy nodes.

carla (support): customers notified. two follow-up tickets created: TCK-3391, TCK-3394.

maya (oncall): final note: root cause likely interaction between kernel-2.1.4 scheduling presets + increased KV cache misses for certain request shapes. devon/sam to confirm. I'll convert this to a post-incident report once RCA done. :white_check_mark:
